clue.text: Is such a message barely conveyed?

definitions.text: Is such a message barely conveyed?

blocks.clueFragment: Is such a message barely conveyed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a message delivered scantily, with hardly any words or detail
setter's reading: the greeting is delivered by a performer who ends up bare, literally undressed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' looks like 'hardly', but it means 'in a state of nakedness': this novelty message is sung or spoken by someone who strips while delivering it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strippergram is a novelty greeting delivered by a performer who takes their clothes off, so the bearer is literally bare.

clue.text: Bible location, a desert almost next to another

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for desert is left off

blocks.note: taken as written
to rat is to desert or betray one's side
another word for desert, the same verb again

explanation.surface: A biblical place described as a stretch of wilderness lying beside another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy noun, but it is the verb, abandon. 'Another' asks for a second helping of that same word, this time complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat is where Noah's ark comes to rest in Genesis, so it is a place named in the Bible.

clue.text: They attract hereditary title-holders getting periodical for nothing

indicators.note: one thing given for another means it is swapped in, taking the place of what it replaces

blocks.note: a baronetcy is a hereditary title ranking below a baron
short for magazine
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Members of the hereditary nobility draw attention by taking a magazine for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For nothing' reads as 'free of charge', but it means the periodical replaces the O in the title-holders.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar magnets are straight rectangular magnets, and magnets are things that attract iron.

clue.text: Topless dish left to get mobbed by admirer

indicators.note: someone mobbed is surrounded by a crowd, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: a fan is an admirer
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A dish with no top is abandoned and swarmed by a devoted follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' seems to ask for a first letter to be dropped, but it is part of the definition: a flan has no pastry lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, a tart with no upper crust, hence a dish without a top.

clue.text: Barmen's way to stop spills

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece fills a hole inside the other

blocks.note: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting, as is a taper
abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A tip from bar staff on how to prevent drinks being spilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spills' suggests slopped drinks but means lighting spills; the street abbreviation is plugged into them after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an old word for someone who draws and serves beer in a tavern, a barman.

clue.text: Court victor in case of assaults, with pardon overturned

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the first and last letters are kept
in a down clue, overturned means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the outside letters of assaults
eh? is what you say for pardon? when you did not hear

explanation.surface: A legal hearing over assaults ends in a win and a pardon is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'case' paint a courtroom, but the court is a tennis court. Arthur Ashe won Wimbledon in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was an American tennis champion who won three Grand Slam titles, a victor on the tennis court.

clue.text: Fly east, twice ignoring areas to the north

indicators.note: twice tells you to write the compass word two times over before taking anything away
ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped
in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards, from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written, and used twice
A is the abbreviation for area; two areas means both A's go

explanation.surface: An instruction to fly east twice, avoiding regions in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the direction word twice, remove both A's for the two areas, then read the result upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African blood-sucking fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Italian side scoffs about out-of-date tickets in Europe

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football team
to rail at is to scoff at or deride
passé means no longer fashionable

explanation.surface: An Italian football team mocks the old-fashioned tickets used across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffs' could be eating, but here it means jeers. The outdated word sits inside the jeering word, after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrail passes are rail tickets giving unlimited travel across many European countries.

clue.text: Decorative art block seen in furniture store

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: the Swedish flat-pack furniture retailer
to ban something is to block it

explanation.surface: An ornamental piece is spotted among the stock of a furniture shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block' looks like a lump of wood or a building block, but it is the verb, prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging, a decorative art form.

clue.text: Priest not considering Catholic Shroud item worth revering

indicators.note: not considering something means leaving it out of account, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a relic is a venerated object, as the Turin Shroud is
RC is short for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A priest dismisses the Shroud of Turin as an object of veneration, regardless of the Catholic view.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters of the Catholic abbreviation happen to be the first and last of the revered object, so removing them leaves the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the priest at Shiloh in the Book of Samuel who raised the young Samuel.

clue.text: Small parts on track inspiring Memories

indicators.note: to part two things is to come between them, so one word separates the other two

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
mini means small
a scent is a trail or track left by an animal

explanation.surface: Tiny components laid on a railway line, bringing back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small parts' reads as 'little pieces', but 'parts' is a verb: the small word comes between the words for on and track.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent calls the past to mind, so it is evocative, prompting recollection.

clue.text: Following answer, Labour leader is going on

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the leader's name is placed after the single letter

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for answer
Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: A Labour leader is leaving, after giving an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' tempts you to take the first letter, L, but it is a former party leader by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means in progress or happening, as in 'something is afoot'.

clue.text: What preachers do goes wrong without fixed spiel

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so its letters are jumbled
without in its old sense means outside, so the first word goes around the second
fixed here means doctored or rearranged, as a rigged result is, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: an anagram of goes
an anagram of spiel

explanation.surface: A preacher's sermon falls flat because it lacks a well-rehearsed patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: one jumbled word wraps around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To gospelise is to preach the Christian gospel to people, evangelising, which is a preacher's work.

clue.text: Revolutionary keeps means to seize power in Crimean city

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read backwards
to seize is to take hold of, so one word grips the other inside it

blocks.note: to save something is to keep it
a tool is a means of doing something
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A rebel holds the means to take control in a city in Crimea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it is an adjective telling you to reverse the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevastopol is the major port city of the Crimean peninsula, famous for its siege in the Crimean War.

clue.text: More than one cooler male wearing jewellery … 18!

indicators.note: something worn is surrounded by the wearer's clothes or jewels, so one word goes inside
the answer at 18-down reads as an instruction to release a word and let its letters go loose

blocks.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a buck is a male deer or rabbit
the first word of the 18-down answer, whose second word says it is to be freed

explanation.surface: A man in his finery is told he is free to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The 18-down answer reads as 'SET free', so its first word is shuffled into a new order; the male sits between the diamonds and that result.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice bucket keeps wine or drinks chilled, so it is a cooler; the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Cut of a thousand pounds pocketed by partner

indicators.note: something pocketed is tucked inside, so the letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
a bride is a marriage partner
G stands for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A spouse quietly takes a share of a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, so it means to cut.

clue.text: One catches school members opening part of dark web after break

indicators.note: the opening part of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
after means placed behind, so the gap word follows the single letter

blocks.note: the first letter of dark
a rift is a break or split
a net is a web of mesh

explanation.surface: A predator lurks among pupils, preying on them through the dark web after the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a shoal of fish, not a place of learning; 'dark web' suggests the internet, but the two words are used separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift net hangs in the sea to trap shoals of fish, so it catches the members of a school.

clue.text: Service Italian vehicles, as some say

indicators.note: what some say points to pronunciation, so a word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: Vespa is an Italian make of motor scooter

explanation.surface: Maintain the Italian motor scooters, as some people suggest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a verb about maintaining vehicles, but it is the noun, a church office. In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening prayer service in the Christian liturgy.

clue.text: E.g. radio engineers plugging heavy metal shortly being released

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one piece is put inside the other
shortly means in abbreviated form, so the metal is given as its chemical symbol

blocks.note: a radio is an example of a set, a receiving apparatus
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a heavy metal
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Radio engineers briefly turn to playing heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests a music genre, but it is iron. RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regular crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Set free means liberated, so it matches released; the definition reads 'being released' as the state that results.

clue.text: My bosses and I developed close relationships

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee says they built a close rapport with their managers.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbiosis is a close, mutually dependent association between two organisms or people; the plural matches 'relationships'.

clue.text: American in senate emptily repeated opening word?

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, a word keeps only its outside letters
in means placed inside, so the American abbreviation goes within the second pair

blocks.note: the outside letters of senate
the same two letters written a second time
standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A US citizen in the Senate keeps saying the same hollow words.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: 'Open sesame' is the password from Ali Baba that opens the cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is the magic word in 'Open sesame!', which opens the robbers' cave in the Ali Baba story.

clue.text: Frequent search to secure backing from America

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one word encloses the letter
the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter is taken

blocks.note: a hunt is a search
the last letter of America

explanation.surface: A regular search to win support from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequent' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to visit often. 'Backing' sounds like support, but it takes the back letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt a place is to visit it habitually, so it means to frequent.

clue.text: Words greeting chess champ's thrashing

blocks.note: hi is a word of greeting
Ding Liren was world chess champion from 2023 to 2024

explanation.surface: Saluting the chess world champion, who has suffered a heavy defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrashing' sounds like a chess loss, but here it is a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a severe beating, so it means a thrashing, either physical or in a match.

clue.text: Lightning fast left back

blocks.note: split is slang for left, departed
to back a proposal is to second it

explanation.surface: A speedy left-back in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' reads as a football position, but each word is a verb in its own right: left is departed and back is support.
explanation.definitionFit: Split-second means happening in an instant, so it describes something extremely quick.

clue.text: In recital, storyteller's instrument

indicators.note: a recital is something spoken or performed out loud, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: a teller of stories, in the sense of fibs, is a liar

explanation.surface: A storyteller plays their instrument at a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' suggests a bard, which fits the instrument nicely, but a 'story' is also a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient stringed harp-like instrument, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Golfer nearly bags an eagle

indicators.note: to bag something is to hold it inside, so the letters sit within the words before

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A golfer almost scores an eagle, two under par on a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golfer nearly' tempts you to shorten a golfer's name like Ernie Els, but the letters lie across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a common crossword bird.

clue.text: Rishi's antagonist putting away energy drink

indicators.note: putting something away removes it from view, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: Keir Starmer opposed Rishi Sunak as Labour leader
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer knocks back an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting away' suggests drinking, which fits the energy drink, but it means removing the letter. Rishi Sunak was UK prime minister until 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine mixed with blackcurrant liqueur, so it is a drink.

clue.text: At one time, retain working woman who lost her head

indicators.note: working means being worked on, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once, a woman kept a job and then lost her composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost her head' reads as panicked, but it is literal: she was guillotined.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Antoinette, queen of France, was beheaded by guillotine in 1793, so she literally lost her head.
